newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Wary Australian stocks end lower, watching Wall St.
newsitem.headline: Wary Australian stocks end lower, watching Wall St.

text.p: The Australian share market ended lower on Friday as cautious traders cut positions ahead of Wall Street's reaction to U.S. inflation data due later today.
The All Ordinaries index shed 12.4 points to 2,380.5.
Brokers said hesitant investors would be keeping an eye on U.S. markets after the U.S. producer price index was released, with Wall Street's reaction likely to set the early local tone next week.
"If the PPI figures are reasonable, U.S. stocks will go up tonight and we will follow suit on Monday," said a dealer at a Sydney brokerage.
"But at this stage the market is just very cautious about these figures coming out."
Other market participants agreed. They said the week's local trading was based on second-guessing the Wallis financial system report issued on Wednesday and tonight's U.S. prices report.
"Today has been more of the same. It has been a week of wait and see really," said one broker, hoping for more substantial action next week.
"We may get more of a trend next week."
Features in a day of reluctant trade were hard to find with Victorian-based regional Bank of Melbourne the pick.

The takeover target lost 1.3 percent to A$9.34 (A$7.38)as nervous traders fretted over the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission's (ACCC) attitude to Westpac Banking Corp's A$9.75 per share bid. The Wallis report retained the ACCC's key role in assessing bank mergers.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about three to two, while about 33 percent of stockS traded remained steady.
